tasks.spec:
You are a code worker. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. Edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit, push or touch .git. Do NOT run a formatter on YAML or markdown (run `uv run ruff format` on Python files you change; if uv is unavailable use the repo .venv python with PYTHONPATH=.). You own only: storygame/story_package/models.py, storygame/story_package/loader.py, storygame/runtime/item_facts.py, docs/markdown-story-authoring.md, docs/world-model-grounding.md, and these tests: tests/test_markdown_story_package.py, tests/test_bench_item_facts.py, tests/test_scoped_aliases.py (new). Edit nothing else; do NOT edit data/stories/* and do NOT edit tests/fixtures/*. No story nouns in engine code (use only synthetic names such as 'crate', 'workshop' in tests).

Background. A world.yaml entity name and aliases become guarded phrases in the narration safety scan in EVERY scene where the entity is not nameable (storygame/runtime/narration_safety.py uses indexes.entity_alias_to_entities, built in storygame/story_package/loader.py from entity_surface_forms). Declaring a thing with common-word aliases therefore rejects ordinary narration in other scenes. A precedent already exists for groups: Group.scoped_aliases (storygame/story_package/models.py), 'plain words that name it only while it is placed and in scene scope; they are not world aliases' (docs/markdown-story-authoring.md). They are checked by the loader (blank or duplicate-of-declared-name is an error, loader.py near line 1090), resolved by ItemFactsProvider._resolve_scoped_group in storygame/runtime/item_facts.py, and never enter entity_alias_to_entities, so they are not guarded anywhere. Tests for the group version: grep tests for 'scoped_alias' (tests/test_markdown_story_package.py, tests/test_bench_item_facts.py `_new_group_scoped_alias_provider` and the three test_group_scoped_alias_* tests). READ those first.

Task: give ITEMS the same optional `scoped_aliases` (and keep groups working exactly as now). Behaviour: for an item, a scoped alias is a plain-word name that resolves to the item only while the item is placed in the current state and is in scene scope (reuse _name_in_scene_scope and the same placement test the group path uses; decide what 'placed' means for an item by reading how the group path uses world.area and how items get their place, and mirror it; state your choice in notes.md). A scoped alias is never added to entity_alias_to_entities, never to the guard index, never to any recall surface-form list. The item's own name and its ordinary `aliases` keep their current behaviour.

Steps.
1. models.py: move `scoped_aliases: tuple[str, ...] = ()` from Group up to a place where Item inherits it too (the Entity base is acceptable if Npc and Location then also accept the field harmlessly; if that makes the field ambiguous, add it to Group and Item only). Existing group data and tests must be unchanged.
2. loader.py: apply the same two validations (blank scoped alias is an error; a scoped alias equal, case-insensitive, to any declared entity name or alias is an error, with the message naming the entity id and kind) to items as well as groups. Do not change the messages for groups that tests assert.
3. item_facts.py: generalise _resolve_scoped_group into a resolver that also returns an item id for an item scoped alias under the rule above. Keep the group results identical. Where the resolver is called, make sure an item match is returned as an item (not as a group) and that two entities claiming the same scoped alias in one scene resolve to none (ambiguity) rather than to the first.
4. Tests, new file tests/test_scoped_aliases.py built on a small SYNTHETIC package (copy how tests/test_leak_terms.py builds one; tests/fixtures/stories has fixtures; use a tmp_path package if simpler). Prove: (a) an item's scoped alias resolves to the item in a scene where the item is placed; (b) it does not resolve in a scene where the item is not placed; (c) narration containing the scoped alias in a scene where the item is NOT placed is accepted by the narration scan (it is not a guard), while narration containing the item's own NAME in that scene is still rejected as an unavailable entity (narration_known_term_leak); (d) the loader rejects a blank scoped alias and one equal to another entity's alias, for an item; (e) group scoped aliases still behave as before (existing tests keep passing unmodified).
5. Docs: edit the existing scoped_aliases sentence in docs/markdown-story-authoring.md in place to say groups and items; add one short bullet to docs/world-model-grounding.md under Things saying: to name a thing with common words in one scene without guarding those words in every other scene, give it a unique name and put the common words in scoped_aliases. No dates, counts or results.

Run: `TMPDIR=/tmp uv run pytest -q tests/test_scoped_aliases.py tests/test_markdown_story_package.py tests/test_bench_item_facts.py tests/test_narration_safety.py tests/test_narration_corpus.py` (the corpus test file may not exist on this branch; ignore that path if it does not). Write ./notes.md with the placement rule you chose, every changed function and the test results.
tasks.verified: items accept scoped_aliases with group behaviour unchanged, scoped alias never guarded, item name still guarded, corpus test unchanged, suite and ruff pass
